metadata.case_name: WONG SIU SHAN v. TSANG HIN SUM

source: Upon admission to hospital, it was found that a deep laceration, 8 cm in length, was present over the vertex.
The laceration was sutured and the Plaintiff was treated conservatively. He was hospitalised for 2 days.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: the Plaintiff was assaulted by the Defendant with a knife and sustained injuries in the head, arm and leg.
the Plaintiff was assaulted by the Defendant with a knife and sustained injuries in the head, arm and leg.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the knee or lower leg, unspecified

manifestations.description: the Plaintiff suffered post-concussional syndrome including headaches, dizziness, fatigue, irritability, difficulty in concentrating and performing mental tasks, impairment of memory, insomnia, and reduced tolerance to stress and emotional excitement.
the aforesaid disability suffered by the Plaintiff is permanent and he also assesses the Plaintiff to have suffered a 3 per cent permanent impairment as a result of the assault.

treatments_future: weekly neurosurgical consultation for 6 weeks (recommended by Dr Yu)
consultation with family doctor on a need basis

losses.description: 3 per cent permanent impairment as a result of the assault.

comparable_cases.case_name: Cheng Lai-kwan v Nan Fung Textile Limited
comparable_cases.injury_description: had sustained only physical injuries to her forehead from which she had made a full recovery; might have suffered 2 per cent disability for post-concussional syndrome; was able to resume her work after a sick leave period of about 41/2 months.
